{{Quote|Ladies and gentlemen, there may be some turbulence up ahead; make sure your seatbelts are fastened!|RX-24, on Star Tours Flight 45 to Endor|<ref name="ST" />}}
'''RX-series pilot droids''' were a line of [[Droid/Legends|droids]] designed and manufactured by the companies [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] and [[Reubens Robotic Systems]]. With a squat, cylindrical chassis that terminated in a flared [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] base for locomotion, RX-series [[Pilot droid/Legends|pilot droids]] used their three clawed [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] to manipulate [[Starship/Legends|starship]] controls and [[Pilot/Legends|fly]] vessels. Units commonly featured brushed metal chassis with [[Color/Legends|colored]] accents. A [[Armor/Legends|helmet]]-like head topped each RX pilot droid, and a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] faceplate&mdash;sporting two glowing [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] and a [[Speaker/Legends|speaker]]&mdash;enabled the droids to more easily interact with organics. RX units were capable of operating independently to pilot starships, especially in tasks that organic pilots found too dull or repetitive to bother with, such as docking and undocking spacecraft, maneuvering cargo between vessels, and piloting passenger craft along well-traveled [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]. The droids' [[Programmer/Legends|programming]] also made them apt copilots and support personnel. They were renowned for their toughness and reliability, although when an RX-series droid failed, it did so spectacularly. A [[Heuristic processor/Legends|heuristic processor]] afforded RX units the ability to creatively solve problems, and when spared from [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]], they tended to develop chipper personalities that allowed them to better interface with living beings.

Industrial Automaton and Reubens Robotic Systems introduced the RX-series pilot droid to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] market by approximately [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. The companies' goal was to create a hybrid [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]]&ndash;[[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] that could not only assist in spaceship piloting and maintenance but also easily interface with organics. The droids proved a success, with most [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] purchasing a few RX units from the line. RX droids saw service during the Clone Wars, as when the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Griebs Kishpaugh]] employed the unit [[Z-37]] to pilot his [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]]. The [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] passenger liner service purchased a crew of RX-series droids to pilot its [[StarSpeeder 3000]] spacecraft on its short-lived service to the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]]. One of those droids, designated [[RX-24/Legends|RX-24]], piloted the initial [[Star Tours Flight 45]] to Endor, but the novice's errors sent his craft through a series of misadventures before returning safely to their point of departure.

==Description==
{{Quote|I'm experiencing some minor technical difficulties... difficulties... difficulties&hellip;|RX-24, upon his first arrival to the Star Tours travel agency|<ref name="ST2" />}}
[[File:RX-24.jpg|left|thumb|RX-series droids had three clawed limbs with which to pilot spacecraft.]]
RX-series [[Pilot droid/Legends|pilot droids]] shared at least some features in common with the [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] produced by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]], such as a cylindrical body.<ref name="SGD" /> However, whereas an astromech [[Droid/Legends|droid]] body was a single width and terminated in three wheeled [[Limb/Legends|legs]],<ref name="AD Enc">{{SWE|technology|astromechdroids|astromech droids}}</ref> the RX [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] droid featured three wide, disc-like sections separated by accordion connecting material and a narrow base that<ref name="Hasbro" /> flared out to form a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] platform. This base afforded RX droids the ability to hover and move at the speed of an average [[Human/Legends|Human]] at a run. The RX-series pilot droid manipulated [[Starship/Legends|starship]] controls and other elements of its environment with three clawed appendages; the multiple limbs also made such droid pilots more versatile than [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], with only two fine manipulators.<ref name="SGD" /> Of the droid's arms, the topmost attached at the left side of the first major body section under the head, the second attached to the right of the middle body section, and the third attached to the right side of the accordion-like base. The arms were articulated in three places: the shoulder, elbow, and wrist. The two right-hand limbs ended in pincer-like gold claws, while the leftmost manipulator featured a thick third digit as well.<ref name="Hasbro" />

The RX head could swivel along a wide arc,<ref name="ST" /> and sufficiently modified, it could be slotted into the chassis of an astromech model, such as the [[P2-series astromech droid|P2-series]].<ref name="TLJ">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']]</ref> It was more humanoid than that of Industrial Automaton's astromech lines. The head was roughly semi-circular, shaped like a domed [[Armor/Legends|helmet]].<ref name="SGD" /> Toward the droid's anterior, the head flattened into a face that sported two [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]]&mdash;[[Color/Legends|colored]] blue<ref name="Hasbro" /> or gold<ref name="TEW" />&mdash;and a round [[Speaker/Legends|speaker]].<ref name="Hasbro" /> Spaced like humanoid [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], the photoreceptors shone a bright white when illuminated; they blinked on and off and the speaker flashed when an RX unit talked. An RX droid could lower a retractable, hinged visor over its photoreceptors.<ref name="ST" /> Each RX droid sported a circle, divided into eight sectors, on each side of the head.<ref name="Hasbro" />

Common color combinations for RX-series droids featured brushed metal for most parts of the droid, accented by gold claws, a gold section at the top half of the face, a gold speaker, and a gold neck ring. Accents in another color were also common, including purple<ref name="Hasbro" /> and red.<ref name="ST2" /> Another color scheme made the entire droid gold.<ref name="TEW" /> The connecting material between body sections was black.<ref name="Hasbro" /> The visor could be purple, red,<ref name="ST2" /> or gold.<ref name="TEW" />

==Role==
{{Quote|Star Tours is proud to introduce the Starspeeder 3000, the most advanced transport of its kind in existence. With high-speed warp drive and a travel range of over one billion light years, the Starspeeder makes touring the galaxy safe and comfortable, and all of our Starspeeders are piloted by the newest, most reliable RX droids, so you can sit back, relax, and enjoy the sights. Whenever your plans call for intergalactic travel, call on the best: Star Tours.|Spaceport announcement before the departure of Star Tours Flight 45 to Endor|<ref name="ST" />}}
[[File:Fitzpaugh_and_his_droid.jpg|thumb|right|RX-series pilot droids flew spacecraft and aided organic pilots.]]
The RX-series pilot droid was a [[Class two droid/Legends|class two droid]], a type intended to assist organic beings with [[Realspace/Legends|spaceflight]] and vehicle or starship maintenance.<ref name="SGD" /> They were designed to serve both as copilots for organics, and as primary pilots in jobs that were too dull and routine for living beings, such as moving supplies from ship to ship and maneuvering docked starships.<ref name="S&V" /> They had a reputation for reliability and durability, since they required only a minimal amount of maintenance. Nevertheless, RX units tended to fail spectacularly in those rare instances when they did break down.<ref name="SGD" /> Another common use for the droids was to conduct passenger flights along well-traveled [[Hyperspace route/Legends|routes]]; tourism agencies in particular employed RX droids in this capacity. The repulsorlift base allowed an RX pilot droid to hover at the level of a starship's controls, where it could employ its three manipulators to operate the vessel. Other [[Programmer/Legends|programmed]] skills included basic starship maintenance, [[Computer/Legends|computer]] use, and knowledge of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[astrography]].<ref name="S&V" /> Although generally not intended for combat, they were able to fire starship weapons and evade attacking vessels when necessary, tasks for which their innate dexterity came into play. Although slightly less perceptive than Humans and similar [[Species/Legends|species]] on the whole, the RX units' sophisticated photoreceptors afforded them keen vision that allowed them to easily distinguish starships in area around them.<ref name="SGD" />

Each unit came equipped with a [[Heuristic processor/Legends|heuristic processor]],<ref name="SGD" /> which allowed it to learn and to solve problems creatively.<ref name="SECR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> The RX-series were made to interact with living beings, so they had generally amicable personalities; especially if their owners chose not to [[Memory wipe/Legends|wipe their memories]], RX-series droids tended to develop personalities more readily than other droids and could become quite charismatic<ref name="SGD" /> and adventuresome.<ref name="CDD">{{SW|url=news/convenient-daily-departures-the-history-of-star-tours|text=Convenient Daily Departures: The History of ''Star Tours''|int=Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours|nolive=1}}</ref> However, their [[Memory bank/Legends|memory banks]] required periodic maintenance to purge them of corrupt and disorganized data.<ref name="CWA">{{TCWA|Droid Programming}}</ref> They had a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] to facilitate communication. By default, the droids spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and [[Binary/Legends|Binary]]. RX-series pilot droids were capable of defending themselves with their clawed limbs if threatened, although such attacks did only minimal damage. Otherwise, their design afforded them strength close to that of most humanoid species.<ref name="SGD" />

Some owners&mdash;especially those not keen to entrust piloting to an automaton but still eager to take advantage of the RX's capabilities&mdash;modified their RX units to serve as [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogation]] droids. Such tinkering required the installation of an [[astrogation buffer]] and, in some instances, a [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]] to allow the RX droid to directly connect to a [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]], access [[Galactic coordinates/Legends|hyperspace coordinates]], and shave [[Time/Legends|time]] off [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]] jumps. RX droids modified in this manner sometimes received a [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|hypertransceiver]] to permit them to plot the hyperspace course through a direct [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] connection. Such modification required additional programming to improve the RX's adeptness at using computers. Another modification altered the RX to serve as a [[Communications droid/Legends|communications droid]], making the unit act like a [[Comm unit/Legends|communications]] [[Computer terminal|terminal]] for the owner. Such alteration required that an internal [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] be added to the droid and routed through the droid's vocabulator and audio receptors to allow the ship's [[Captain/Legends|captain]] to use the droid to hail other vessels. The typical range for a droid thus modified was generally 200 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], unless the owner added a hypertransceiver as well. A final type of modification turned the RX into a [[tactical systems droid]], able to manipulate the ship's onboard systems to maximize performance. Such a change entailed replacing one clawed appendage with a Human-like hand, affording more fine motor coordination to manipulate on-board utilities. As an alternative, the addition of a scomp link permitted the droid to [[Slicer/Legends|jack]] directly into the ship's systems. To be truly effective as tactical systems units, RX droids also needed an upgraded [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] package. Some owners opted to replace piloting-related programming to make room for such modifications.<ref name="SGD" />

==History==
{{Quote|Hey, sorry, folks. I'm sure to do better next time&hellip; It ''was'' my first flight, and I'm still getting used to my programming!|RX-24, at the end of Star Tours Flight 45|<ref name="ST" />}}
[[File:Defective_RX-24_SWI127.jpg|thumb|left|upright|The pilot droid RX-24 was defective upon his first arrival at the Star Tours travel agency.]]
The RX-series hit the [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] market by approximately [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="TEW" /> Both [[Reubens Robotic Systems]]<ref name="CSWE III" /> and Industrial Automaton (IA) were companies involved in the design and manufacture of the droids. IA in particular designed the RX-series to bridge the gap between the astromech and [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] markets<ref name="SGD" /> by not only programming them to pilot vehicles but also providing them with the capacity to interface directly with passengers.<ref name="S&V" /> To that end, IA's designers chose to replace the dome-shaped head common among astromech droids with a more humanoid head to which organics could better relate.<ref name="SGD" /> The droids retailed for between 7,300 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]<ref name="S&V" /> and 9,855 credits,<ref name="SGD" /> and most [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] purchased at least a few RX-series droids to help move docked starships, pilot supply [[Skiff/Legends|skiffs]], and take chartered flights through well-traveled regions. Other customers could purchase the droids with a proper license.<ref name="S&V" />

Around 22 BBY, during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Griebs Kishpaugh]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] employed an RX-series droid designated [[Z-37]]. When a group of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] under Kishpaugh's command were shot down on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Oznek]], they traveled by foot to their target, a [[Oznek power plant|power plant]] run by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]&mdash;unbeknownst to them, Kishpaugh had one of the [[Cloning/Legends|clones]], codenamed "[[Ghost (clone trooper)|Ghost]]," act as his personal agent to destroy the power plant and anger the inhabitants of Oznek into joining the Confederacy, with whom the Commander was secretly aligned. However, [[Trooper/Legends|trooper]] [[Banks (clone)|Banks]] discovered the ruse, [[Death/Legends|killed]] Ghost, and impersonated him in an encounter with Kishpaugh aboard the Commander's [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]]. During their encounter, Kishpaugh accidentally shot and destroyed the RX-series droid before it could launch the craft and allow its master to escape.<ref name="TEW" /> During the same conflict, the astromech droid [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] reprogrammed an [[Unidentified RX-series pilot droid (Galactic Republic)|RX-series pilot droid's]] memory banks to purge them of corruption and disorganization.<ref name="CWA" /> A few years later, in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Technician/Legends|technician]] [[Geri]] and his team salvaged an RX-series head and fitted it to a P2-series droid chassis. The resulting hybrid, named [[Candy (droid)|Candy]], aided the Rodian in his shop on the planet [[Toprawa/Legends|Toprawa]].<ref name="TLJ" />

The [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] [[Klikk]] knew of an [[Unidentified RX-series pilot droid (Naboo)|RX-series droid]] that had a spectacular malfunction on the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Its [[Unidentified RX-series pilot droid owner|owner]] had just stepped down from a starship [[Entry ramp/Legends|boarding ramp]] when the RX flew away with the ship. The [[Naboo system/Legends|Naboo system]] [[Naboo system observation post|observation post]] launched [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] to stop the wayward automaton, but they failed to catch it before the ship jumped to hyperspace, its course consistent with hyperlanes leading to the planets [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]], [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]], and [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]].<ref name="SGD" />

RX droids were frequently used as pilots by space tourism companies.<ref name="S&V" /> Indeed, the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency used them aboard their [[StarSpeeder 1000]] passenger [[Transport/Legends|transports]], and later [[StarSpeeder 3000]]s,<ref name="ST2" /> as early as [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]]. The company's first shipment of RX-series droids were defective, but rather than return them, Star Tours opted to have its in-house repair droids fix them back up.<ref name="CDD" /> One droid form this shipment was [[RX-24/Legends|RX-24]].<ref name="ST2" />
RX-24, nicknamed "Rex," was repaired<ref name="ST" /> in house<ref name="CDD" /> by [[4 ABY/Legends|4.3 ABY]],<ref name="LC blog">{{Blog|holocron|7|Death Star timeline}}</ref> when he was tasked with conducting the [[Star Tours Flight 45|maiden voyage]] of the Star Tours agency's new StarSpeeder 3000 passenger starship<ref name="CSWE III" /> to the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="CSWE III 189b">{{CSWECite|III|189|Star Tours Travel Agency}}</ref> The flight nearly proved disastrous when the droid's beginner's mistakes brought the starship into the midst of a field of [[Water/Legends|icy]] [[Comet/Legends|comets]], a [[Battle of Death Star III|battle]]<ref name="ST" /> between [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="ST date">The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] had transitioned to become the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] by 4.3 ABY according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] forces, and an attack run on an [[Death Star III|Imperial battlestation]]. Nevertheless, Rex's deft piloting allowed him to escape the perils into which his inexperience had cast him and his passengers.<ref name="ST" /> Within a few [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of Rex's flight,<ref name="G9">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref> the Star Tours travel agency was driven out of business by similar accidents and poor management.<ref name="CSWE III 189b" /> Besides RX-24, two other RX-series pilot droids existed during the early stages of the Galactic Civil War: [[RX-23/Legends|RX-23]], a red-colored RX-series pilot droid, and [[HHG-RX]], the latter of whom spent most of his time hitch-hiking at [[Spaceport THX1138]].<ref name="ST2 Tokyo">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]'' (Tokyo version)</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Is Star Tours basically like a commercial flight simulator?''"''<br />''"''Well, it is like that. But this is a little more adventurous than that. Most airline simulators don't have the problems that Rex, our pilot, has&hellip; considering this is his first flight.|An audience member and George Lucas at the Star Tours opening press conference, [[January 9]], [[1987]]|<ref name="Endor">{{EndorExpress|url=special-features/opening-day-press-conference|text=Opening Day Press Conference}}</ref>}}
[[File:1986StarToursPoster.jpg|thumb|right|upright|RX-24 was one of the stars of the theme park ride ''Star Tours''.]]
RX-24, the first RX-series droid in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], was designed as the pilot for the joint [[Lucasfilm]]&ndash;[[The Walt Disney Company|Walt Disney Company]] attraction [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']], for Disney's [[Disneyland]] theme park in [[Wikipedia:Anaheim, California|Anaheim, California]]. Because the ride was designed as a spaceflight simulator, the creative team decided to tailor the ride experience to being on a passenger liner, with all action experienced in the first person. Such a premise necessitated the creation of a relatable narrator and guide to engage the audience throughout the ride's duration. ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] suggested that a droid pilot might be able to serve that function, and he proposed a droid version of the skippers of the [[Wikipedia:Jungle Cruise|Jungle Cruise]] ride in Disneyland's [[Wikipedia:Adventureland (Disney)|Adventureland]] area in the 1980s;<ref name="SWI104">{{InsiderCite|104|Star Tours: Taking Off on a Star Tour|''Star Tours'': Taking Off on a Star Tour}}</ref> the droid version would be a sardonic Clone Wars veteran.<ref name="CoGL">''[[The Cinema of George Lucas]]''</ref> [[Tony Baxter]], the director of the ride's development,<ref name="SWI104">{{InsiderCite|104|Star Tours: Taking Off on a Star Tour|''Star Tours'': Taking Off on a Star Tour}}</ref> suggested instead that the droid be more nervous than cynical, a jumpy neophyte pilot whose errors set the conflict of the story in motion. The team developed the idea into Captain Rex.<ref name="SWI104" />

Based on preliminary ideas from Lucas, Disney [[Wikipedia:Walt Disney Imagineering|Imagineer]] [[Chris Runco]] created a prototype Rex puppet in green foam. [[Larry Sheldon]] and [[Lance Updyke]], two other ride designers, then crafted the Rex puppets from aluminum based on Runco's design. Four separate animatronic Rexes were created to man each of the four different StarSpeeder 3000s available to visitors to the Star Tours ride when it opened in [[1987]]. As the attraction was recreated and expanded upon in various Disney theme parks, further RX-24 pilots were constructed as well.<ref name="SWI104" />

For years, Rex remained the only droid of his kind in ''Star Wars'' continuity. In [[2008]], however, the [[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']] sourcebook for the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook|Saga Edition]] of the [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' presented the RX-series pilot droid as a product line manufactured by Industrial Automaton&mdash;and as a possible character choice for players of the game.<ref name="S&V" /> However, the 2008 compendium ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' makes no mention of IA and instead states that RX-24 was manufactured by Reubens Robotic Systems.<ref name="CSWE III" /> [[2009]]'s ''[[Scavenger's Guide to Droids]]'' includes an expanded description of the RX-series and supports ''Scum and Villainy''{{'s}} attribution of the model to IA.<ref name="SGD" /> This article assumes that both companies had some role in the history of the line's manufacture.

RX-series pilot droids have also featured in non&ndash;''Star Tours'' sources. The mini-game "Droid Programming," part of the [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online game|massively multiplayer online game]] [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Clone Wars Adventures'']], features an RX unit in the level "Delete Type." In that stage, the player attempts to clear a screen of color blocks, which represent the memory banks of the RX-series droid.<ref name="CWA" /> The [[2012]] graphic novella ''[[The Clone Wars: The Enemy Within]]'', written by [[Jeremy Barlow]], features the RX-series droid Z-37.<ref name="TEW" />

In [[2005]], Lucasfilm and Disney set out to update ''Star Tours'', setting the [[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue|new version]] of the ride in the time period between [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. Because Rex had stated that he was undertaking his first flight in the original ride, set much later in the ''Star Wars'' timeline, the Lucasfilm&ndash;Disney team created a new droid pilot, [[AC-38/Legends|AC-38]], for the revamped attraction. Nevertheless, the designers placed several RX-series pilot droids along the queuing area beside crates. Most bear stickers marking them as "defective,"<ref name="TIJ">{{InsiderCite|127|The Incredible Journey}}</ref> and one&mdash;RX-24 himself&mdash;sparks at the neck and mutters lines from the original attraction.<ref name="ST2" /> The attraction opened to the public in [[2011]].<ref name="StarToursReturns">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/Star_Tours_Returns_Starting_May_20th_136170.asp|text="Latest News - Star Tours Returns Starting May 20th"|author=Eric|date=2011-01-18|archivedate=20190729153331}}</ref>
